Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 Hz/40 fps on the LCD gives perfectly smooth motion for this pace-varied shooter. High textures keep the remake looking its best while FSR recovers the render cost of the upscale.

profiles.Summary: Black Mesa, the fan-made Half-Life remake running on Source engine, is well within the Steam Deck's capabilities given its modest PC requirements (GTX 960-class minimum). It runs under Proton with a gold ProtonDB rating and should deliver smooth performance at medium-to-high settings without heavy tuning.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from Black Mesa's PC minimum requirements (GTX 960-class GPU) and the Source engine's historically light GPU demands. On your first run, check frame rate in the outdoor Xen chapters — those are the heaviest areas — and drop to the Optimal profile if you see sustained dips below 40 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Dropping to 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a 6 W TDP cap keeps the Deck cool and quiet for long sessions. Source engine is CPU-friendly, so the low GPU clock is the main lever here.

KnownIssues: No native Linux build; runs via Proton — occasional shader compilation stutters on first play-through are possible

No Deck-specific player reports found; behavior is estimated from PC requirements and Source engine characteristics

MaxPerformance.Notes: Source engine is lightly threaded and GPU-light enough that the Deck can push native 1280x800 at high settings near 60 fps in most areas; expect brief dips in the most complex outdoor Xen sections. Multicore Rendering should be enabled in the Advanced options if available.

Optimal.Notes: Rendering at 1024x640 upscaled via FSR gives a clean image at 60 fps with medium-to-high textures — the sweet spot for Source engine on Deck. Textures are set to High since the Source engine is not VRAM-hungry, while shadows and shaders are kept at Medium to ease GPU load in Xen.

profiles.Summary: Black Mesa is a Source engine remake of Half-Life that runs well on the Steam Deck, with the older engine keeping GPU demands modest enough for smooth play at medium-to-high settings. No dedicated Deck reports were found, but the Source engine's light footprint and the game's minimum specs suggest comfortable performance without heavy tuning.
profiles.BasisNote: No dedicated Steam Deck or Proton player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the Source engine's known efficiency, the game's PC minimum/recommended specs (which the Deck comfortably meets), and the Deck's GPU class. On first run, check frame rate in a Xen level (the most demanding area) and step down Shadow Detail or resolution if you see sustained dips below your target.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a 6 W TDP cap keeps the battery going well over four hours. Low settings and a locked 30 fps ensure the APU stays cool and power draw stays minimal; Xen sections may dip briefly but the cap keeps it stable.

KnownIssues: Partial controller support means some menus or UI elements may require touchscreen or trackpad navigation.
Proton compatibility is rated Gold/Playable, so occasional minor rendering glitches or launch issues may occur.
The Xen chapters are more GPU-intensive than the original Black Mesa sections and may cause frame dips.
No native Linux build; runs through Proton, which may add minor overhead or occasional stutters on shader compilation.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Source engine is old enough that the Deck can push high/very-high settings at native 1280x800 and hit the 90 Hz cap in most areas. The Xen chapters with dense foliage and water reflections may dip to the 60s, so consider dropping Shadow Detail to Medium if that occurs.
